name: Technical Writing Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for technical writing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for technical writing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate technical writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. When technical writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Prefer the simplest technical writing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Before starting technical writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. When technical writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen technical writing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Measure before optimizing any technical writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated technical writing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new technical writing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop technical writing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about technical writing over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
